teaser.text: Cardinal Health sits between the companies that make healthcare products and the places where patients receive care. To understand its business, follow the dollar from a manufacturer to a provider, through Cardinal’s warehouses and services, and back out as supplier payments, operating costs and profit.

blocks.heading: Where could Cardinal Health's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts the shares at $249.26 in October 2027, a 1% loss including dividends. It reaches $294.24 in October 2029, an 18% gain. The cases carry 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull probabilities.

The central case is modest near-term upside, with a wide outcome range by year three. The weighted price is $249.26 in October 2027, a negative 1% return with dividends. It rises to $270.81 in October 2028, an 8% return. By October 2029 it reaches $294.24, an 18% return. The October 2029 range runs from $178.35 in the bear case to $477.99 in the bull case. Today's price is $254.06.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Cardinal Health?

paragraphs.text: Earnings are the main source of value, and the base case assumes continued but moderating improvement. Management guides FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS to $12.40–$12.60. The supplied next-twelve-month EPS estimate is $14.07392, supporting $3,280M of normalized earnings. The base case then uses $3,670M and ends at $4,100M. This reflects Pharma profit growth, Other segment growth and better recurring contributions from specialty products, while excluding unusual items.

The bear case starts at $2,850M, then reaches $3,000M. It ends at $3,150M because generic erosion, weaker GLP-1 demand and lower post-refund GMPD profit offset specialty growth. The bull case starts at $3,500M and reaches $4,000M. It ends at $4,570M, requiring guidance to be exceeded, repeatable GMPD profits and successful integration of acquired platforms.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Cardinal Health really make?

paragraphs.text: Cardinal pays manufacturers and collects from pharmacies and health systems, but those events do not occur together. Working capital is the money temporarily tied up in receivables, inventory and payables. In fiscal 2026, accounts payable released $3.463 billion of cash, while receivables and inventory absorbed cash. The result was much more than accounting profit simply translated into dollars.

dividend.title: Cardinal Health dividend: cash coverage and history
dividend.meta_description: Cardinal Health pays $0.5158 quarterly; fiscal 2026 cash covered its $491 million dividend, while buybacks, acquisitions and debt competed for cash.
dividend.opening: Cardinal Health currently pays $0.5158 per quarter and has raised annual dividends by $0.02 in each of the five years supplied. Cardinal Health's cash covered the dividend: it generated $5.2 billion of operating cash flow, spent $649 million on capital expenditures and paid $491 million in dividends in fiscal 2026.
dividend.closing: The full Cardinal Health memo also answers how Cardinal Health's business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could affect it.

blocks.heading: How much does Cardinal Health pay shareholders over time?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise cautiously in the base case. The current quarterly rate is $0.5158, and the company has raised annual dividends by $0.02 in each of the five years supplied. The base case pays $2.07 in the first window and $2.11 in the second. It reaches $2.15 in the final window, allowing for debt, settlement obligations and uneven cash conversion.

blocks.heading: Does Cardinal Health's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Cardinal generated $5.2 billion of operating cash flow in fiscal 2026, but spent $1.9 billion on Solaris, $649 million on capital expenditures and $491 million on dividends. The stock’s past valuation matters because the market is paying for that future cash, not merely for sales.

The pattern is clear even without treating free cash flow as a dedicated acquisition fund. Cardinal paid regular dividends and repurchased shares, while acquisition spending exceeded internally generated cash in its heaviest spending year. Debt issuance helped bridge that gap, moving the company from net cash to net debt; it remained a net debtor after the following year’s cash generation.

blocks.heading: What could change Cardinal Health's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The forecast moves toward the bear case if FY2027–FY2029 results show generic erosion, weaker GLP-1 demand or Pharma profit growth below guidance. GMPD profit that fades after the tariff benefit would reinforce that move. Working-capital reversals or settlement payments that constrain buybacks would further weaken per-share growth.

blocks.heading: What is Cardinal Health's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Revenue is not profit in this business. Cardinal buys medicines from manufacturers and delivers them to pharmacies, hospitals and other care providers. Most of each sales dollar belongs economically to the manufacturer, so Cardinal may keep only a small amount for distribution, services and operating profit. That makes its 0.2x price-to-sales ratio less informative than its margins, earnings and cash flow.

blocks.heading: What has Cardinal Health guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: For the year ending June 2027, management guides to $12.40–$12.60 per share. It describes that as 13%–15% growth from tariff-adjusted FY26 EPS of $10.95. The reported FY26 non-GAAP figure was $11.26, including a $0.31 one-time tariff refund, so the comparison deliberately removes that windfall.

Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions is guided to 3%–5% revenue growth and 8%–11% segment-profit growth. Global Medical Products and Distribution is guided to 2%–4% revenue growth and $200 million–$220 million of segment profit. The smaller “Other” group is expected to grow faster, but its scale is different: the main pharmaceutical segment generated $234.8 billion of FY26 revenue, while Other generated $6.8 billion.
